req.title: Return 404 on unknown post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-022 requires HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or POST /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id. The test suite must cover: (1) positive case — a logged-in user accessing update/delete on an existing post gets 200/302, not 404; (2) negative case — accessing update/delete on a non-existent post id returns exactly 404; (3) boundary case — post id 0 (below minimum valid id) and post id 21 (one above the highest seeded id=20) both return 404. We also test both HTTP methods (GET and POST) for update, and POST for delete. Login is performed via POST /auth/login using seeded credentials. The exact status code 404 is asserted (not >= 400) to catch comparison-operator mutations. Both update and delete endpoints are exercised to catch mutations that might only fix one branch.

tests.name: test_update_existing_post_returns_200_not_404
preconditions: Database seeded with 20 posts; post id=2 authored by user id=1 (Rahul/stone)
User Rahul is logged in
expected: HTTP 200 (not 404) — existing post is found and update form is rendered
trace: R-FLASKR-022: positive path — existing post must NOT return 404
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_existing_post_returns_200_not_404():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200

test_update_existing_post_returns_200_not_404()

tests.name: test_update_unauthenticated_nonexistent_post_redirects_not_404
preconditions: Database seeded with 20 posts; post id=9999 does not exist
No user is logged in (anonymous session)
expected: HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login — login_required fires before get_post, so 404 is NOT returned for unauthenticated requests
trace: R-FLASKR-022: decision table — login_required decorator intercepts before get_post; unauthenticated access redirects, not 404
